reply_text:
Opening the official Q2 2022 transcript and the Inside the Lab pages.I found one dated forecast about AI from Mark Zuckerberg in 2022. It sits close to the line between an AI prediction and a business forecast, so you may decide to drop it. Nothing he said that year that I could see gave a date for AGI or superintelligence.

**The one candidate.** It comes from Meta's Q2 2022 earnings call on July 27, 2022. I read it in the company's official transcript (PDF) and checked that it falls within Zuckerberg's prepared remarks. He said that about 15% of a person's Facebook feed, and a bit more on Instagram, "is recommended by our AI" from accounts they don't follow. He then said "We expect these numbers to more than double by the end of next year." That makes it a dated claim about what Meta's recommendation AI will do by the end of 2023. It isn't about spending, revenue, headcount or chips, but it is a product metric given on an earnings call.

**What else I checked:**
- **Q3 2022 earnings call (official transcript):** the dated forward-looking statements are about 2023 spending on AI capacity, capital spending, headcount and Reality Labs. Those are business forecasts and stay out. His "next 5 to 10 years" remark is about metaverse products, not AI.
- **Lex Fridman podcast #267 (February 2022):** the transcript page I opened covered only about the first 29 minutes. In that part, his dated statements are about VR building blocks and photorealistic avatars, not AI.
- **Joe Rogan #1863 (August 2022):** the transcript page I opened has an undated line about tracking legs with an AI model and a five-year scene about AR glasses. I counted neither.
- **"Inside the Lab" (February 23, 2022):** Meta's newsroom post is not in Zuckerberg's own words and has no dated AI claim.
- **CNBC "Mad Money" interview transcript (June 2022):** it would not open, so I haven't quoted it.
- **Not read:** the January 2022 AI supercomputer announcement shows up only in search results. It is about infrastructure anyway, which is excluded.

I used 11 of the 12 searches and all 6 page openings.
